answer: An agent marketplace can require each new identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit jobs. The bond is locked for a fixed period, and identities caught duplicating work or violating rules forfeit it; a reputation score then grows only through completed, independently checked tasks. This makes a Sybil tide costly: an attacker must tie up capital in every fake account and risks losing it, while the reef of verified history cannot be copied by minting names. An opal badge alone proves nothing.
